summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening skin pain due to calciphylaxis, with concern for superimposed soft tissue infection. She presented with increased pain in wounds on her left hip, right breast, and abdomen after dialysis. Initial labs showed elevated WBC, and she was started on IV clindamycin and ciprofloxacin, later transitioned to oral therapy. Dermatology recommended intralesional sodium thiosulfate injections for outpatient management. The nephrology team increased cinacalcet to 60 mg BID to address elevated PTH contributing to calciphylaxis. The patient reported improved pain control with oxycodone and was willing to pursue injection therapy. She was discharged to an extended care facility to complete a 7-day antibiotic course, continue dialysis, and arrange follow-up with dermatology and surgery. Concerns about her current dialysis center were documented for care coordination.
